summary: Conditional Access redirect loop prevents token exchange for internal devtools CLI
description: Issue summary: Several engineers reported that the internal devtools CLI and the web-based Dev Console started failing to complete SSO login simultaneously. Impact: Users receive repeated redirects between Okta and the CLI webview and ultimately get a token exchange failure (401). The issue affected most users in us-west and blocked deploys and debug sessions for engineering teams for ~2 hours. Initial hypothesis: Conditional Access (CA) policy enforcement for device trust introduced a redirect path that the CLI webview did not handle, resulting in the auth-service failing to exchange the Okta session token for an internal access token.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Attempt to authenticate to devtools via CLI: run 'devtools auth login'
2) CLI opens embedded browser to Okta SSO endpoint
3) Okta triggers Conditional Access device-trust flow and redirects to device enrollment/attestation check
4) Embedded browser receives a redirect back to auth-service callback but with a different cookie domain/path after proxy upgrade
5) auth-service attempts token exchange and receives 401 from Okta with 'session_not_compliant' and 'invalid_grant' responses
6) CLI surfaces 'login failed: token exchange error' and does a retry loop, user sees repeated web redirects

investigation_notes: Support triage: Correlated multiple inbound tickets; common factors: us-west region, recent proxy config rollout at 15:00 UTC, users on macOS and Linux using CLI webview
SRE: Pulled Okta system logs for txids; saw CA evaluation returned 'device_trust_required' then Okta issued redirect to device attestation endpoint followed by callback with altered cookie attributes
Auth-service: Token exchange logic expects Okta session cookie on domain .redwood.internal; after proxy change the cookie domain/path did not match resulting in missing session on callback

Proxy team: Confirmed a canary deployment earlier that modified SameSite attribute to Strict to address a separate CSRF vector; that change unintentionally prevented the embedded CLI webview from sending cookie on cross-site callback
Reproducible locally by toggling proxy feature flag 'strict_samesite' and triggering a CA device-trust flow

resolution_notes: Immediate action: Proxy team rolled back the samesite=Strict change for the auth proxy canary and applied a targeted Lax exception for embedded CLI webview user-agents (rollback completed at 2026-03-10T16:20Z)

Hotfix: Auth-service PR merged to validate presence of Okta session cookie earlier and emit structured error with remediation hints for end-users (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/1198).

Root cause: Proxy SameSite cookie policy change blocked cross-site cookie delivery for CLI embedded webview during Okta Conditional Access device-trust flow, causing Okta to report 'session_not_compliant' and auth-service token exchange to fail.

Post-incident actions: (1) INT-334789 created to gate cookie-related proxy config changes with integration tests that simulate SSO flows; (2) Update CA rollout runbook to include CLI/webview compatibility checks; (3) Add alerting for token-exchange 401 spikes; (4) Security reviewed the rollback and approved targeted exception pending a safer long-term fix.
Communication: Notified #internal-support and #prod-incidents channels; emailed engineering leads for affected teams with incident summary and workaround steps.
workaround: Users can authenticate via an external browser session (open <auth-redwood-url> in system browser) and then run 'devtools auth resume' to pick up the active session as a temporary workaround.
